measures.what_it_does: Authorizes up to $51 million of 30-year general obligation bonds, repaid by an annual property tax, to expand and renovate Newport Community Hospital: a new three-story wing, relocated entrance, a larger emergency department with behavioral health rooms, more operating rooms and more imaging, lab and therapy space. The same bonds failed in the August primary with 45.2% yes; 60% is needed.
measures.cost_line: Estimated $1.47 per $1,000 of assessed value a year for up to 30 years, about $36.75 a month on a $300,000 home. District taxpayers can apply for up to $750 a year in credits toward hospital bills.
measures.pro_summary: The statement for (Taylor Stewart, JoAnn Bell, Kevin McNamee) says the bond keeps emergency, therapy and specialist care close to home instead of in Spokane or Coeur d'Alene. Hospital leaders say the 1958 wing is at capacity and that waiting would raise the $55 million cost; the Newport City Council passed a resolution supporting it, 2-1 with one abstention.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was submitted. Voters rejected the same bonds 2,084 to 1,719 in August. About 30% of the hospital's patients live in Idaho.

taxes.basis: A yes vote adds a new 30-year excess property tax of about $1.47 per $1,000, well above the district's current levies.

spending.basis: A yes vote expands hospital capacity and services (more emergency beds, operating rooms, new services, 20-25 jobs).

measures.sources_note: Local voters' pamphlet pp. 14-15 (S1); VoteWA measure 7307 (S2); Spokesman-Review (S3, S4) and Miner (S5-S7) coverage; August primary results (S8); PDC (S9); DOR 2025 levy detail (S10); RCW 39.36.020 (S11).

measures.what_it_does: Replaces Riverside School District's educational programs and operations levy, which expires at the end of 2027, with a three-year levy for 2028-2030. It pays for electives and advanced courses, vocational education, nurses, counselors, technology, safety, arts, athletics and activities, about 13% of the budget. Only the district's Pend Oreille County part votes on this copy.
measures.cost_line: Estimated $1.58 per $1,000 of assessed value: $3,996,811 in 2028, $4,116,715 in 2029 and $4,240,217 in 2030. The expiring levy is about $1.52 per $1,000.
measures.pro_summary: The statement for (Community for the Riverside Replacement Levy: Jeni Vineyard, Kevin Koesel, Jennifer Gaffaney) says it replaces the current levy rather than adding one, and funds courses, nurses, counselors, safety, arts and athletics that are 'not extras' to students.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was submitted; the pamphlet says no volunteers came forward. Voters rejected a separate Riverside capital levy in 2025.

taxes.basis: A yes vote continues an existing school levy at a slightly higher estimated rate ($1.58 vs. $1.52 per $1,000); a replacement, not a new tax.

measures.sources_note: Local voters' pamphlet pp. 16-17 (S1); VoteWA measure 7332 (S2); Spokesman-Review (S3); DOR 2025 levy detail (S4).

measures.what_it_does: Levies a one-year property tax for the Sacheen Lake Water and Sewer District's general fund, to pay for aquatic weed control, lake-level management (including beaver-dam clearing), upkeep of the Myers/Harter sanctuary and insurance. Voters around the lake have approved the same levy every two years. Needs 60% approval.
measures.cost_line: About $0.75 per $1,000 of assessed value, $113,827 in total, collected in 2027 only; the 2025 levy was $0.73 per $1,000.
measures.pro_summary: The statement for, by Sacheen Lake Association president Grant Miller, says the levy funds weed treatment that keeps invasive weeds from choking parts of the lake, at no additional tax cost.
measures.con_summary: The statement against, by 'a concerned citizen', says: 'I should not be taxed to provide revenue for a government organization. It should be my choice.'

taxes.basis: A yes vote renews a one-year excess levy at about the current rate ($0.75 vs. $0.73 per $1,000).

measures.sources_note: Local voters' pamphlet pp. 18-19 (S1); VoteWA measure 7245 (S2); DOR 2025 levy detail (S3); SOS precinct results 2020, 2022, 2024 (S4-S6); RCW 84.52.052 (S7).
